abertura: Before a meeting, people often send a short update by email.
Three of these sentences are true about a useful update. Mark the three.

itens.t: It is short enough to read before the meeting.
itens.porque: People read it in a few minutes, often just before the meeting starts.

itens.t: It tells the whole history of the project from the start.
itens.porque: The reader needs what changed now. The history can come later, if someone asks.

itens.t: The subject line says what the email is about.
itens.porque: The subject line helps the reader decide if they need to read it now.

itens.t: You need to read it two times to find the main point.
itens.porque: In a useful update, the main point is easy to find the first time.

itens.t: It tells the reader if they need to do something.
itens.porque: An update often ends with a request: an answer, a decision or a date.

itens.t: It is only useful if the reader agrees with it.
itens.porque: An update gives information. The reader can disagree and still use it.

sec2.pt: Escolha o sentido que cada palavra tem num e-mail de trabalho. As seis palavras estão no e-mail que você lê na aula.

doc.titulo: From: Carla · To: Everyone on the second floor
doc.texto: Hi everyone, the printer on the second floor is not working. A technician can come on Wednesday. Until then, please use the printer on the first floor. If you need to print a lot of pages, send me the files by 3 p.m. and I can ask the print shop to do it. Thanks, Carla

abertura: Read the message once. Three of these sentences are true. Mark the three.

itens.t: The printer on the second floor is broken.
itens.porque: “the printer on the second floor is not working.”

itens.t: The technician is coming today.
itens.porque: The technician “can come on Wednesday”, not today.

itens.t: People can use a different printer for now.
itens.porque: “Until then, please use the printer on the first floor.”

itens.t: Carla wants everybody to stop printing.
itens.porque: She gives two other ways to print. Nobody has to stop.

itens.t: The print shop can help with big print jobs.
itens.porque: If you need a lot of pages, Carla can ask the print shop.

itens.t: The message is about buying a new printer.
itens.porque: The message is about a broken printer and what to do this week. It says nothing about a new one.

sec5.pt: Complete cada frase com uma palavra ou expressão da atividade 2. As opções estão no quadro acima das frases.

sec6.titulo: A meeting you have at work
abertura: Write a short note about a meeting you have at work.

callout.texto:
Who is in the meeting? What do you usually explain, answer or ask there? What is difficult for you in English in that meeting?

You can change names. You can use your note in your lesson.

sec6.pt:
Escreva uma nota curta sobre uma reunião que você tem no trabalho.

Quem participa? O que você costuma explicar, responder ou perguntar nela? O que é difícil para você em inglês nessa reunião? Você pode trocar os nomes, e pode usar a sua nota na aula.

itens.t: The laptops were supposed to arrive last Friday.
itens.porque: “The new laptops for the sales team did not arrive last Friday.”

itens.t: The training is canceled.
itens.porque: Nobody canceled it. Moving the training is only one of the two options.

itens.t: The supplier had a problem at the warehouse.
itens.porque: “The supplier had a problem at their warehouse.”

itens.t: Ryan already chose one of the options.
itens.porque: He did not. “I need a decision by Monday.”

itens.t: The training is before the new delivery date.
itens.porque: The training is next Tuesday, and the delivery is now next Thursday.

itens.t: The supplier needs an answer by Monday.
itens.porque: Ryan needs the decision, so he can tell the supplier and the trainer.

tf1.rationale: Two of the false sentences are easy to believe: nobody canceled the training, and it is Ryan, not the supplier, who needs the decision.

itens.t: The new laptops for the sales team did not arrive last Friday.
itens.porque: It tells Paula the fact: the laptops are not here.

itens.t: The supplier had a problem at their warehouse, and the delivery is now next Thursday.
itens.porque: Still what happened: the reason for the delay and the new date.

itens.t: The sales team has training on the new system next Tuesday.
itens.porque: On its own it is only a date. Next to the delivery date, it is the problem: Tuesday comes before Thursday.

itens.t: Without the laptops, they cannot practice with the system in the training.
itens.porque: It says what goes wrong if nothing changes.

itens.t: We move the training to the following week, or the sales team uses their old laptops.
itens.porque: Two possible solutions, joined by or.

itens.t: I need a decision by Monday, so I can tell the supplier and the trainer.
itens.porque: The request, with a date. It is what Paula has to act on.

cl1.rationale: Two lines tell what happened, two say why it is a problem, one gives the options and one says what Ryan needs. Paula can follow the email because the parts come in this order.
